# Practitioner Academy Proposal: Tamarack Instruments (fictional)

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel
**Program:** Practitioner Academy, AI Governance Academy
**Format:** 2 days, live virtual, four 90-minute working sessions per day
**Price:** US$12,500

## Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. The Client is headquartered in the Netherlands, operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States and has about 1,100 staff. Its AI maturity is at the piloting stage.

The Client has three AI use cases:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

The regulatory drivers are the EU AI Act and GDPR. Work toward ISO/IEC 42001 is planned to start next year, and the start date is not fixed. The incumbent frameworks are an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS, an ISO 9001 quality management system and an internal audit function. An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded no inventory of AI systems.

Dana Whitfield has stated the objective: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

Three constraints shape this design:

- Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.

## Why Hands-On Practitioner Capability Fits Now

The Practitioner Academy is built around participants doing the work themselves. Over two days, the General Counsel, CISO, Head of Quality, Head of Data, German plant manager and two internal auditors work directly in the GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) and the Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen). They leave with artifacts already started and know where each instrument lives.

The timing aligns with three dated facts:

- The June 2026 finding concerns an AI system inventory, and Session 2 starts one.
- The Q2 2027 objective centers on visual inspection, which runs through both days as a worked example.
- ISO/IEC 42001 work is planned for next year. Artifacts started in the program can feed that work, though the program makes no certification or audit outcome promise.

The program teaches three principles: Slow AI, Informed Intent and Final Liability rests with the Human.

- **Slow AI:** AI that cannot be governed, explained and audited is not deployed; the three tests are conjunctive, and the doctrine is a precondition, not a speed limit.
- **Informed Intent:** no AI system acts without prior authorization stating its purpose, authority, boundaries and exit, given by a human who meets the five authorizer conditions.
- **Final Liability rests with the Human:** every material outcome attaches to a named human owner with decision rights, oversight and the power to intervene.

## Running Worked Examples

**The customer service chatbot and AI visual inspection are the two running examples. AI sales forecasting is a third, lighter example.**

- **Chatbot:** It is the one deployed system. It lets participants work the EU customer data constraint and GDPR through sanitized analogs.
- **Visual inspection:** It is tied directly to the stated Q2 2027 objective. It also brings the works council constraint into oversight design.
- **Sales forecasting:** Because it is planned, participants can practice inventory entry and new-system intake before any build.

## Curriculum Spine and Exercises

Day 1 uses the GRC Workbook. Day 2 uses the Slow AI Kitchen plus assurance references: The Definition of Done (https://github.com/rolldabones/definition-of-done) and AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards).

*The Turtle and the Phoenix* is told in Session 1 from its facilitation kit (https://github.com/rolldabones/AI-Governance-Academy/blob/main/the-turtle-and-the-phoenix.md). This seats the doctrine before the instruments arrive on Day 2, and the kit's handle map bridges the story to the workbook modules.

| Session | Exercise | Repository asset | Artifact produced |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fable told; handle map links story to modules; teams draft decision rights for chatbot and visual inspection | GRC Workbook, governance structures module; facilitation kit, handle map | Draft decision-rights map by role for both systems |
| 1 (close) | Kit's twenty-minute closing exercise, worked on the running examples | Facilitation kit, section 8 | The three artifacts of the kit's section 8 |
| 2 | Enter the three use cases; classify each against the EU AI Act and GDPR as working positions for counsel review | GRC Workbook, AI system inventories and classification module | Started AI system inventory with three entries |
| 3 | Assess risk and impact for chatbot and visual inspection; data protection screening for the chatbot on sanitized analog data | GRC Workbook, risk and impact assessments module | Draft risk register entries for both systems; chatbot impact screening |
| 4 | Draft an AI use policy outline and a new-system intake procedure, tested on sales forecasting; list touchpoints with ISO/IEC 27001 and ISO 9001 documentation as questions for their owners | GRC Workbook, policies and operating procedures module | Policy outline; draft intake procedure |
| 5 | Write and test governed prompts for chatbot support scenarios using synthetic customer queries | Slow AI Kitchen, governed prompting pattern | Governed prompt specification for the chatbot |
| 6 | Design end-to-end workflows on paper: chatbot escalation to a human agent and visual inspection result handling, using sanitized analog inspection cases | Slow AI Kitchen, practical AI workflow design pattern | Governed workflow 1 (chatbot); governed workflow 2 (visual inspection) |
| 7 | Write an Informed Intent authorization for each workflow; name owner roles; place intervention points; mark a works council consultation gate before any step that touches production staff | Slow AI Kitchen, human oversight and accountability pattern | Two authorization records; oversight and intervention map |
| 8 | Walk through all artifacts with the two internal auditors as reviewers; set evidence and acceptance criteria; map upward reporting to the board layer | GRC Workbook, evidence collection and audit readiness module; The Definition of Done; AI Governance for Boards | Evidence checklist and acceptance criteria per workflow; owner list for finishing each artifact |

## Deliverables

Participants leave with the following, each started in the repositories during the program:

- A started AI system inventory.
- Draft risk register entries for the chatbot and visual inspection.
- Two governed workflows with authorization records.
- A policy outline and intake procedure.
- An evidence checklist.
- The three artifacts of the facilitation kit's section 8.

## Logistics and Price

**Format:** The program runs live and virtual over two days, with four 90-minute working sessions each day.

**Dates:** Unknown, to be set at intake.

**Data handling:** No real customer data is used. Chatbot exercises run on synthetic, clearly labelled analogs. Visual inspection exercises are design work on sanitized analog cases and make no change to the production line or to production staff.

**Price:** US$12,500, within the budget approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.

## Questions to Confirm at Intake

1. What dates and daily time window suit all participants?
2. Should the German works council be informed or consulted before the visual inspection exercises run in the program?
3. Is there an existing risk register to receive the draft entries, and who holds it?
4. Who will own finishing each artifact after the program?
5. Who will prepare the sanitized analog material, the Client or the facilitation team?
6. What is the confirmed start date for ISO/IEC 42001 work?

## Next Step

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. The proposed next step is an intake call with Dana Whitfield to settle the questions above. The pre-work packet would then be issued to participants.

Human-made, for Easy Work, Simply Done.
